title: Express Intent test reading through page objects

intentCoverage.report:
Verdict: Caught. The maintained assertion caught loss of the selected source target after a replacement file read failed. This verdict covers that failed-read transition before Retry; it does not claim faulted retry completion or whole-suite coverage.

Story: SEED-300#express-dashboard-test-intent-through-page-objects, .planning/seeds/SEED-300-dashboard-test-page-objects.md, key example “A selected source line survives a revision notice or failed read.” Checked revision: 816db4660de6bcc813a1941544a452a21cce0c18. The supplied story worktree was isolated on codex/express-intent-test-reading-through-page-objects with a clean index and worktree before the probe.

Fault: In dashboard/src/IntentFileReading.tsx:127, temporarily add `|| failedRevision !== undefined` to the condition that makes targetLine undefined. This plausible production regression discards the selected case target while displaying retained source beneath a failed replacement read. Fixtures, assertions and test helpers were unchanged. The saved original bytes were restored in a finally block, with signal handlers arranged before mutation.

Fixture and maintained proof: dashboard/tests/intent/intent-source-target-recovery.spec.ts, the “failed then retried” case, uses MakeMe repository revisions and selects candidate real-h264-codec-roundtrip in tests/test_clip_core.py at independently supplied line 44. The original revision is d4 repeated 20 times; the replacement is f3 repeated 20 times. It holds the replacement source answer, fails that answer, observes retained original text and the exact failed-read revision message, and normally retries to the new source. Its source-file, target-line, revision, focus, reading-offset and request-sequence expectations remain explicit.

The identical focused command was used for baseline, fault and restoration: `caffeinate -s -i npm run test:dashboard -- tests/intent/intent-source-target-recovery.spec.ts --grep 'failed then retried' --workers=1`. Each run selected and executed exactly one test, with no retries. The maintained proof-record destination differed per invocation. The host was on AC power with 48 GiB RAM and 46–47% free memory; external load was elevated, so the run used one worker. Default test and assertion budgets were unchanged.

Observed sequence: baseline passed; the deliberate fault failed; exact restoration passed. The catch was dashboard/tests/intentCodeBrowsePage.ts:39, `expect(target).toHaveCount(1)`, called from intent-source-target-recovery.spec.ts:153 after the failed-read alert. It received zero target rows. This earlier count assertion caught the regression before the later exact-line, aria-current and viewport assertions.

Independent reach and wrong-behavior observation: reconstructed retained Playwright trace DOM snapshots using its postorder node references, without using the helper's locator verdict. Snapshot 231 before the failure showed line 44, `def test_clip_segments_h264_reencodes_video():`, carrying class `source-line is-target` and `aria-current=location`. Snapshot 236 after the failed-read transition showed the same line and text with only class `source-line`, zero target rows and zero current-location rows. The DOM simultaneously displayed “tests/test_clip_core.py could not be read at revision f3f3f3f; showing d4d4d4d. Retry”, source metadata at d4d4d4d, retained `assert True`, and no replacement `assert 2 == 2`. Thus the intended failure path was reached and the actual reader lost its target while retaining the source.

Restoration: production source bytes and mode restored; SHA-256 5a47075c8b441924136545bb4f50052f872d6400cef308c4665221ce55cc3043 matches the saved original. Final HEAD remains 816db4660de6bcc813a1941544a452a21cce0c18, both Git diffs are empty and git status is clean. The restored focused command passed. Only this probe's retained fault-output directory was removed after copying its trace and evidence outside the checkout. No commit, push, stash, default-checkout edit or peer-worktree edit occurred.

Evidence artifacts: /var/folders/65/16p4k5qj42qg7l46k2j0nhj40000gn/T/seed300-intent-coverage-ptus1_6s contains baseline.json, fault.json, restored.json, fault-trace.zip, fault-report.txt, wrong-behavior-witness.json and restoration.json. The report stdout is captured at /tmp/seed300-intent-coverage-report.txt.

Next proof action: retain this exact-target recovery check in the maintained focused gate. The observed failed-read transition needs no stronger assertion for this fault; any wider promise assessment belongs to the caller.

Prior disposition: this evidence matches the already-maintained G7 line44 recovery proof added during the story. It does not create a new repair decision, and no test repair was made by this probe.

- **Test runtime.** 43.040051 seconds total (measured), summing maintained runner durations: baseline 14.358510 s, fault 16.172975 s, restored 12.508566 s. The corresponding test-attempt durations were 9.976 s, 13.583 s and 9.707 s, totaling 33.266 s. Basis: each completed proof record's terminal.durationMs and attempt.durationMs.
- **Human effort.** Unavailable: no separately timed human labor measure was supplied or observed during this probe.
- **Agent effort.** Unavailable: no independent active-agent effort, CPU or token meter was available; invocation elapsed is not substituted for that measure.


- **Invocation-to-report elapsed.** 258770 ms (measured), from 1794444267000 to 1794444525770 in Unix epoch ms. The end clock was sampled after writing the prepared report body.


## Wrap-up disposition

Checked revision: 816db4660de6bcc813a1941544a452a21cce0c18.
The independently observed failed-read target loss was caught by maintained proof;
retain the exact-target recovery case and its independent call-site facts. No
new test repair, product defect, or follow-up is created by this deliberate fault.
Scope remains that one failed-read transition, not the whole story or faulted Retry.
Exact source and clean checkout restoration, plus the restored pass, are verified.
The separate retrospective cleanup SEED-318#remove-unused-taken-comparison-navigation
with plan .planning/slice-plans/596-remove-unused-taken-comparison-navigation/PLAN.md
will be queued first under the existing default disposition; it addresses an
unused test API and does not claim to repair this already-protected behavior.
